The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) intends to issue a brand-name call under the DHS Strategic Sourcing Vehicle (SSV) Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) Medical Supplies II, referred to as MedS2, for Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Automated External Defibrillators and associated

ts limiting the requirement to the Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 brand-name product and associated accessories pursuant to RFO 16.507-7. This justification does not authorize award to a single BPA holder without competition. The resulting RFQ/call will be competed among eligible DHS Strategic Source Vehicle Blanket Purchase Agreement Medical Supplies II (MedS2) BPA holders capable of providing the required Stryker brand-name supplies. Only the Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 brand-name product can meet the Government’s minimum needs; however, multiple eligible BPA holders may be capable of providing that product. FEMA intends to procure a brand-name specification for Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) and associated accessories. The exception is based on RFO 16.507-7 because the Stryker LIFEPAK CR2 cellular AED platform provides the combination of clinical, operational, remote monitoring, and deployment features required to meet FEMA’s mission needs. FEMA personnel and emergency response teams deploy across the United States to austere disaster environments, including Joint Field Offices, Long-Term Recovery Offices, regional locations, temporary duty locations, and disaster field operating locations. These environments may lack municipal power, reliable local Wi-Fi

ailable, unreliable, or restricted. This minimizes or eliminates pre-shock pauses and increases compression time during cardiac emergencies. This capability is essential to support effective emergency cardiac response for deployed FEMA personnel. c) High-energy biphasic shock output. Operating out of production plants in Albany, Georgia, and Barstow, California, MDMC serves as the Marine Corps' principal industrial capability, executing complex rebuilds, modifications, and repairs that extend the service life of critical weapon systems. By delivering high-quality, combat-ready ground equipment back to the warfighter, MDMC directly enhances the operational reach, survivability, and lethality of the Marine Air-Ground Task Force (MAGTF) globally. Marine Depot Maintenance Command augments the Fleet Marine Force with advanced manufacturing and maintenance capacity to support Marine Corps operational objectives. 1.3 Objectives: The overall objective of this contract is to secure contracted service augmentation enabling Marine Depot Maintenance Command to sustain its core competencies in depot maintenance, production, logistics, engineering, facilities, and business operations, in support of Fleet Marine Force readiness (see Background above). Individual task orders may draw on any combination of these competencies. 1.4 Scope: The scope for this contract is to provide technical, administrative, analytical, engineering, logistics, maintenance, inspection, testing, calibration, fabrication, facilities maintenance, inventory management, production support, quality assurance, program management, and other related services necessary to support MDMC operations.
